DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. Mr. BERNARDO M. NICOLAS, JR. Chief Operating Officer Consolidated Mines Inc. Units 901 B & C State Center II Bldg., Ortigas Ave. Mandaluyong City Dear Mr. Nicolas: This refers to your letter dated August 22, 2023, requesting this Department's opinion on Resolution No. 241-20 of the Sangguniang Bayan of Masinloc (Declaring Mr. Alfonso A. Paz, Consolidated Mines Incorporated (CMI) — Officer-in-Charge (OIC) as "Persona Non Grata" in the Municipality of Masinloc, Province of Zambales). In your letter, you represented the following: CMI is currently renewing its Mineral Production Sharing Agreement over a mining site located at Masinloc and Candelaria, Zambales. Pending such renewal, CMI was tasked by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources with the care and maintenance of the Coto Mines premises, including all its auxiliary area[s] and facilities. Allegedly, the Sangguniang Bayan of Masinloc and the Office of the Mayor are "vocal oppositors" to CMI's application for renewal, such that even Alfonso Paz, who was CMI's OIC over its mining site, was compelled to leave the Municipality by reason of the subject Resolution declaring him to be Persona Non Grata, as well as repeated verbal harassment by certain members of the LGU upon the issuance of said Resolution. Premised from the foregoing, you posit the following queries: I. What is the nature of the aforesaid Municipal Resolution declaring Alfonso Paz as Persona Non Grata? Does it carry with it the force of law? 2. May the declaration of Persona Non Grata by a local sanggunian compel an employer to remove its personnel or officers from his/her work premises located within the LGU's territorial jurisdiction? 3. Does the declaration of Persona Non Grata by the Sanggunian of Masinloc over the person of Alfonso Paz physically prevent him from traveling to and from the Municipality of Masinloc? 4. Does the declaration of Persona Non Grata by the Sanggunian of Masinloc over the person of Alfonso Paz prevent him from discharging his functions as an employee of CMI within the Municipality of Masinloc? "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

We note that the foregoing queries are fundamentally interrelated, and as such, we deemed it apt to address such queries in one discussion. Foremost, it is to be noted that the declaration of persona non grata is generally applied to aliens in the context of diplomatic relations. The term "persona non grata" is a Latin phrase that means "an unwelcome person". Such a practice of declaring a person/persona non grata is enshrined in the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. A diplomat who is no longer welcome to the government to which he is accredited is barred from remaining in the country and declared as persona non grata. 1 Along this line, it is worthy to revisit the nature of a sangguniang resolution. In the case of Municipality of Paranaque v. V.M. Realty Corporation (G.R. No. 127820, dated 20 July 1998), the Supreme Court clarifies that: "A municipal ordinance is different from a resolution. An ordinance is a law, but a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matter. An ordinance possesses a general and permanent character, but a resolution is temporary in nature. Additionally, the two are enacted differently- a third reading is necessary for an ordinance, but not for a resolution, unless decided otherwise by a majority of all the Sanggunian members." (Emphasis supplied). Accordingly, a sangguniang Resolution is not a law but rather an expression of sentiment, or merely the form in which the legislative body expresses its sentiment. This Department has, time and again, opined that a sangguniang resolution is not a law but a mere expression of sentiment, or merely the form in which the legislative body expresses its sentiment. On that score, a sangguniang resolution declaring individuals as persona non grata is merely an expression or declaration of the sentiments or opinions of the August Body. Applying this in the subject Resolution, such piece of legislation is merely a declaration of sentiment over Mr. Alfonzo Paz, who in the perception of the Sangguniang Bayan of Masinloc is uncooperative and has shown gross disrespect to the authority of the legislative body. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 30, Series of 2020, dated February 7, 2020, the Department emphasizes that while the local sanggunian may pass a resolution declaring its sentiment—such as declaring certain individuals as persona non grata— the same must be done within the bounds of law. That is, if such declaration is their way of expressing their sentiment, that is perfectly within their authority. However, if such declaration would already engender Mr. Alfonzo Paz from doing his functions as an employee of CMI, then this is already reprehensible. Notwithstanding, it is to be noted that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government, and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measures enacted or passed by local government officials, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials that are alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out before the proper forum. 1 DILG LO No. 30 series of 2020 dated 7 February 2020 Page 2 of 2

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
